# map

#### Course: Modern JavaScript Essentials

## map

While forEach performs actions, map transforms. It runs a function on each element and builds a brand-new array with the results.

For example,

```javascript
1const scores = [80, 45, 92, 67]; 
2const doubled = scores.map(score => score * 2);
3
4console.log(doubled);
```

Here, map creates a new array where every score is doubled. The original scores array stays untouched. It is good practice to choose map whenever you need a transformed copy and forEach when you only need to perform an action. Keeping this distinction clear prevents bugs where you expect a return value from forEach and get undefined instead.
